A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Joint Embedding Variational Bayes by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the substantially revised method and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-learning experiments, one-class CIFAR-10 anomaly-detection results, and likelihood and loss-component ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original representation-learning, posterior-geometry, and OOD-detection results, alongside additional ablations and computational measurements in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The directional loss changes from an ambient Student-t density on normalized-vector differences to a spherical construction using a geodesic log-map, tangent-space covariance, and an exponential-map Jacobian. v2 also implements and evaluates an EMA target variant and introduces ImageNet-specific variance centering. These change the training procedure, beyond explanatory elaboration.

E1.justification: One-class CIFAR-10 anomaly detection is replaced by full-CIFAR-10 in-distribution training and external OOD evaluation against CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, MNIST, SVHN, Textures, and Places365. Tiny ImageNet representation-learning experiments are also added. CIFAR-100 and STL-10 were already evaluated in v1's ablations.

E2.justification: v2 adds reproduced VI-SimSiam comparisons and reported OpenOOD comparisons with MSP, ReAct, KNN, and ViM. The one-class comparison containing GEOM, DROCC, Deep SVDD, SimpleNet, PANDA, and CutPaste disappears. Rot+Trans, GOAD, and CSI remain under the new OOD task; the ImageNet comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Representation training changes from MoCo-v2 to BYOL augmentations, weight decay from 5e-6 to 5e-4 with exclusions, and default ν from 3 to 1. The 800-epoch comparison changes k-NN from k=30 to k=20 and permits method-specific baseline recipes. The new OOD protocol uses 200 epochs and separate near/far AUROC aggregates instead of ten one-class evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 adds posterior-geometry analysis, factorized-versus-standard likelihood diagnostics, Monte Carlo sample ablations, isotropic-versus-diagonal posterior tests, and compute profiling. The projection-head experiment and joint β-by-ν anomaly sweep disappear. Tail and loss-component ablations are revised, with the directional-only and radial-only configurations removed.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging already appears in v1. v2 extends standard-deviation reporting to the representation comparisons and retained ablations, adds uncertainty bands to OOD curves, and explicitly identifies non-finite-run exclusions and single-run diagnostics. The PDFs do not establish an increase in the existing three-run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 65.6 ± 0.4% with 68.2 ± 0.3% under revised training. The 90.3% one-class AUROC is removed, while the new OpenOOD task reports 92.4 ± 0.2%. Revised ablations show partial collapse at ν=50 on CIFAR-10/100, unlike v1. Changed methods and protocols prevent interpreting these as controlled gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the extrinsic-density argument with geodesic, Schur-complement, tangent-determinant, and Jacobian derivations. Section 4.4 reformulates the variational bound in terms of conditional log-mass under a subprobability model. Appendix B also revises its claimed cosine-objective reduction to accommodate the changed geometry.

C1.justification: The central claim changes from a normalized representation-space likelihood to a spherical subdensity with an associated variational bound. The abstract and introduction replace the claim of outperforming comparable one-class anomaly baselines with broader OOD validation. Competitive representation learning and feature-wise uncertainty remain central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting uncertainty statistics to class geometry and likelihood factorization to collapse prevention. Removing KL is now interpreted through partial learning and seed-dependent instability rather than uniformly failed representations. The conclusion newly distinguishes representation-space uncertainty from calibrated downstream predictions and removes the earlier ImageNet-gap tradeoff discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands implementation specifications with the exact MLP structure, activations, bias choices, initialization, variance transformation, and ImageNet variance centering. Test-time posterior-mean scoring is explicit. Appendix C.4 adds GH200 hardware, batch size, precision, FLOP-counting tools, profiling procedures, and memory-extrapolation information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused discussion of variational contrastive learning, supervised contrastive learning, and SNGP. New spherical-geometry and OpenOOD references accompany the revision, while several one-class references disappear. The principal positioning relative to JEPA-style objectives, VI-SimSiam, and VSSL remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, model explanation, theoretical narrative, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized around representation quality, posterior geometry, OOD detection, ablations, and synthesis. Appendix A gains implementation subsections, and a new Appendix C organizes supplementary diagnostics.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from one CIFAR-10 trajectory plot to three dataset panels. The anomaly-grid heatmap disappears, while posterior visualizations, ROC curves, score distributions, and diagnostic plots are added. Comparison tables are restructured, and separate loss-performance and variance tables become a combined display.

improvement.justification: Direct factorization, sampling, and anisotropy tests in Appendix C address important gaps in v1's support for its central design choices. Reproducing VI-SimSiam, documenting failed runs, and expanding implementation details substantially improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the lost experiments, although the revised theory needs correction: Appendix B.4 claims a constant Jacobian under isotropy, contradicting the angle-dependent expression in Eq. (25), so its exact cosine-loss reduction is unsupported.
